lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: precise definitions of angle, circle, line, and segment
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: precise definitions of angle, circle, line, and segment

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

steps: Fix a centre and a distance.
Take every point in the plane at that distance.
workedSolution.answer: the set of points at a fixed distance from a centre

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. With the compass set to the radius, mark successive arcs around the circle from a starting point, then join consecutive marks. What has been constructed?
choices: a regular pentagon inscribed in the circle
a regular hexagon inscribed in the circle
a square inscribed in the circle
an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle

items.prompt: A regular quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle of radius 4. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: The construction relies on the angle being acute.
Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.
The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a angle?
choices: the amount of turn measured in degrees
a corner of a polygon
the figure formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint
the space between two intersecting lines

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. From vertex V draw an arc crossing both rays at P and Q. From P and Q draw equal arcs meeting at R. Draw ray VR. What has been constructed?
choices: the perpendicular bisector of PQ only
a line perpendicular to one ray
the bisector of the angle at V
an equilateral triangle on PQ

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: A regular quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle of radius 2. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the perpendicular bisector construction?
choices: Both constructed points are equidistant from the endpoints, and the locus of such points is exactly the perpendicular bisector.
Any line through the midpoint is a perpendicular bisector.
The compass width was more than half the segment, which forces perpendicularity.
The arcs look symmetric, so the line must be perpendicular.
